finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.ts::monotonic guard mixes two different clocks (yorkie `issuedat` vs. backend `now()`), so a backend-side bump can permanently block later webhook bumps under clock skew
evidence: The mechanism is real as written: `touchUpdatedAt` gates on `updatedAt < at` (document.service.ts, `updateMany where updatedAt: { lt: at }`), and `at` is derived from Yorkie's `issuedAt` clamped with `Math.min(issuedMs, now)` in yorkie-event.controller.ts:56-58, while `updateDocument` (document.service.ts) and the migration/`@default(now())` write the backend's clock. So any value stored from the backend clock (rename/move PATCH, row creation default, or the NaN fallback) can exceed a lagging Yorkie server's `issuedAt`, in which case subsequent `DocumentRootChanged` events are silently no-ops (count ignored, 200 returned, no log). The design doc's "Clock skew" section indeed only reasons about future-skewed events, so the symmetric past-skew case is unhandled. Impact is bounded by the skew magnitude (typically ms on NTP-synced clusters) and self-heals once wall-clock passes the stored value, so this is a minor ordering-staleness bug rather than the "permanent" block the wording suggests.
